question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Samsung's next mid-range star, the Galaxy A57, has just appeared on a European retailer's website, complete with official-looking renders, and they give us a closer look at what to expect. The images show the phone from multiple angles, confirming a design that aligns perfectly with previous leaks. The Galaxy A57 sports a sleek flat display up front and a vertical triple camera setup on the back, neatly housed in a pill-shaped module. Samsung keeps its signature key island button layout and minimalist rear, while slimmer bezels give it a modern clean look. Though renders sometimes downplay bezel size. The appearance of these retailer renders hints that Samsung is gearing up for an official launch. The Galaxy A5X lineup is usually refreshed in March, and leaks suggests the A57 could arrive alongside the Galaxy A37, with the A27 coming shortly after. Under the hood, the Galaxy A57 packs a 6.7-inch Full HD+ Super AMOLED display with a 120Hz refresh rate, powered by Samsung's Exynos 1680 chip. Buyers can expect 6 gigabytes, 8 gigabytes, or 12 gigabytes of RAM paired with 128 gigabytes or 256 gigabytes of storage. Early benchmarks suggest this new chip delivers a noticeable boost in multi-core performance over its predecessor. Photography won't disappoint either. A triple camera system includes a 50MP main sensor, 12MP ultrawide, and 5MP macro lens, along with a 12MP front shooter for selfies and video calls. Rounding out the package is a 5,000 mAh battery with 45W fast charging, running Android 16 and Samsung's One UI 8.5 right out of the box. According to a claim shared by Winfuture's Roland Quandt on Blue Sky, the Galaxy A57 is reported to launch in five stylish shades: Charcoal, Icy Blue, Gray, Lilac, and Navy, while the Galaxy A37 may arrive in White, Charcoal, Gray Green, Lavender, and Navy, all part of Samsung's signature Awesome Color theme. The Galaxy A57 is shaping up to be a stylish, powerful, and future-ready mid-range option, and these official-looking renders only make us more excited for its launch.

A news report from Al Jazeera discusses France's strong show of military and political support for Cyprus, in coordination with Greece. French President Emmanuel Macron's visit to Cyprus, accompanied by military hardware including the Charles de Gaulle aircraft carrier, is framed as a claim for European primacy in the Eastern Mediterranean. Macron states that an attack on Cyprus is an attack on Europe, emphasizing a unified defense stance. The report highlights a recent European military response, led by Greece, to a drone strike on a British base in Cyprus. It also touches on the broader trend of European defense autonomy, citing a report on increased European arms exports, with France as a leading exporter. The ideological and economic messages of the visit are also explored, stressing the protection of European territory, trade routes, and economic interests, while suggesting a reduced reliance on the United States for security. The reporter, John Psaropoulos, files the report from Paphos Airforce Base in Cyprus.

### Speech Content

**Narrator:** France declared its presence unmistakably with the French presidential aircraft's arrival on Cyprus and the presence of its frigate and the Charles de Gaulle aircraft carrier nearby. Together with the Greek Prime Minister, President Emmanuel Macron was claiming European primacy in the Eastern Mediterranean.

**Emmanuel Macron (Voiceover):** Coming here with the Greek Prime Minister, I want to say that an attack on Cyprus is an attack on Europe. And the defense of Cyprus is a vital issue for your neighbor and friend, Greece, but it is also a vital issue for France and for Europe.

**Narrator:** Greece was the first mover, sending two frigates and four F-16s within 24 hours of a Shahed-type drone striking the British military base at Akrotiri. That has triggered a European response. The leaders of Greece and Cyprus came to deliver messages of solidarity and autonomy, that the security of Cyprus is the security of Europe, and that Europe is capable of providing for its own security. That European presence here is set to grow in the coming days with the arrival of ships from Italy and Spain, because as the French president said, its credibility is crucial for achieving de-escalation. Both leaders strongly support European defense autonomy, and a new report from the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute on Monday revealed that Europe is moving in the right direction. It increased its arms exports by 36% in the last five years, faster than any other region, and now owns 28% of the world's export market for weapons. France, with its Rafale fighter jet and missile systems, leads European exporters, something showcased here with a French helicopter bought by Cyprus. And a state-of-the-art frigate Greece sent here was just delivered from French shipyards. But the ideological message was equally important.

**Greek Speaker (Voiceover):** It's an initiative that in practice breathes new life into this article of the treaty. Because if not now, when? If we don't act together in such a crisis, how will we face possible future crises? Now is the time to make it clear that every inch of European territory cannot be violated.

**Narrator:** And so is the economic message of this high-profile visit, that Europe will keep waterways open for international trade and energy flows. After Russia's war in Ukraine and decades of wars in the Middle East, it is determined to protect its economy from inflation. question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Imagine building one of the most advanced artificial intelligence systems in the world, and then suddenly being labeled a national security risk by your own government. This is exactly what's happening right now between Anthropic and the United States Department of Defense. But what exactly happened? Anthropic is one of the fastest growing AI companies in the world, and it created the AI assistant Claude, a powerful system designed to compete with the most advanced AI models available today. However, the company has always taken a strong position on one important issue, how its AI should be used. So what is the problem between Anthropic and the US government? The conflict reportedly started when Anthropic refused to allow certain uses of its AI technology. For example, the company says its systems should not be used for fully autonomous weapons, and it also rejects large-scale domestic surveillance applications. But why would that create such a big conflict? Because advanced AI has become extremely valuable for military and defense applications. Governments around the world are racing to integrate artificial intelligence into their security systems, and that brings us to the most surprising part of the story. What did the Pentagon actually do? The US Department of Defense labeled Anthropic as a supply chain risk. This designation is very serious. It can effectively prevent a company from working with US defense agencies and government systems. In fact, reports say federal agencies were instructed to begin phasing out Anthropic technology from their networks. So, how did the company respond? Anthropic strongly rejected the decision and argued that the move is unfair and unjustified. According to the company, the government is punishing them for refusing to weaken safety protections on how their AI can be used. Because of that, Anthropic has now taken the fight to court. The company is asking a federal judge to overturn the Pentagon's decision. And this raises an even bigger question. What makes this case so important? If the lawsuit moves forward, it could become one of the first major legal battles between an AI developer and the US government. And the outcome may shape the future of artificial intelligence. So the real question is this, who should control powerful AI systems? The governments that want to use them, or the companies that build them? Let me know what you think in the comments. And follow Creations Tech for more stories about the technologies shaping our future.

Weight is expected to come in around 68 grams with color options spanning black, silver, titanium, and orange. The design sticks with the round form factor used on the Watch X2 and there's a rotating crown alongside a second side button for hardware navigation. The Watch X2 already stood out for its endurance, so a bigger cell in the X3 would only strengthen that reputation. Oppo seems to be taking what already worked and turning up the dial in a few specific areas. For now, the March 17th date is the one to watch.

answer: So in my last video, I talked about some leaked specifications of the Nothing Phone 4a and Nothing Phone 4a Pro. And as we already know, both of these phones are launching on the 5th of March. Now, while we still have more than a week left for the official launch, Nothing has finally shared the design of the phone 4A. So, this is our first look at the Nothing phone 4A and as we can see the design is pretty impressive. I will even say that this is one of the best looking phones that Nothing has ever launched, if not the best. The back has a transparent design like other Nothing phones and there is a horizontal triple camera setup. Now, even though it seems like there is an LED strip around the camera module, there is in fact no LED strip at all on this phone. This time Nothing has added a Glyph bar on the back. Basically, there are six squares on the right side of the camera module with each square having nine individually controllable mini LEDs. Nothing says it went with this Glyph bar design to reduce the distractions since the design is less distracting than the previous versions. Moreover, the lights are now 40% brighter than the phone 3A series. As for the rest of the design, we can see that the Nothing Phone 4A has an extra button on the left side, which should be the essential key which we have already seen on previous Nothing phones. We already know that apart from this white color option, the Nothing Phone 4A is also coming in blue, pink, and black. So, it would be interesting to see how the phone looks like in all those colors, especially the pink one, since I think it is the first time we are getting this color option in a nothing phone. As far as the specifications are concerned, it is almost confirmed by now that the Nothing phone 4A has the Snapdragon 7s Gen 4 chipset. It is also said that this time there is UFS 3.1 storage, which if true will be a big upgrade from the UFS 2.2 storage in the last year's phone 3A. The phone is reported to have a 1.5k flat OLED panel with a 120Hz refresh rate, and there is 50 watt fast charging support. The battery size should be around 5,000 mAh or even 5,500 mAh. And finally, the Nothing Phone 4A will feature a proper triple camera setup on the back with one of the cameras having a telephoto lens. While we had a telephoto camera on the Nothing phone 3A, it had only 2X optical zoom. This time we are expecting at least 3X optical zoom on the Nothing Phone 4A. And well, that is all we know. Personally, I really like the design of the Nothing phone 4A and it is much, much better than what we got with the Nothing phone 3 last year. All that is left now is the pricing and if nothing nails that one as well, then the Nothing phone 4A seems like a balanced mid-range smartphone. So, what do you think of the design? Do let me know via the comment section below and as always, I'll catch you in the next one.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Flat-headed cats have been successfully detected and filmed in southern Thailand for the first time in almost 30 years. One of the world's rarest cats, it was last documented here back in 1995, leading some to believe it was possibly extinct. Conservationists, however, thought otherwise. We had heard reports for many years and were confident that the species was still present. Rettapan Padinarinsen, conservation program manager for Panthera Thailand, told IFL Science. What was needed was the right study design to confirm it. The largest ever survey of the species began in 2024, using camera traps from Thailand's Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation, and Panthera Thailand, a global wildcat conservation organization. 13 detections were made in 2024, and a further 16 detections were made in 2025. Most exciting of all, the observations included a female flat-headed cat with her cub. Flat-headed cats are the smallest in Southeast Asia. They weigh half that of a typical domestic cat and have a distinctive flattened forehead and elongated skull. They are small, nocturnal and prefer to occupy dense terrain, making searching for them in the wild that much harder. Even catching them on camera traps can be difficult. But using lessons learned from studying fishing cats, Panthera were able to identify the best sites for camera placement, leading to the successful detection and photographic evidence of the flat-headed cat. It's estimated there are 2,500 flat-headed cats globally, and they're classed as endangered by the IUCN, but in Thailand, it was considered possibly extinct. A new Panthera-led IUCN assessment is now expected in 2026.

answer: A controversial new budget draft was withdrawn on Thursday morning after thousands of protesters took to the streets of Sofia to oppose it the night before. The government had proposed to increase social security contributions and double dividend taxes in an ambitious new budget, which would have set a new spending record at around 46% of GDP, as well as dramatically increased public debt. Wednesday evening's rally was organized by the opposition coalition and is estimated to have drawn around 20,000 people. Protesters gathered outside the National Assembly building, where lawmakers convened to examine the proposed budget. They formed a massive human chain around the parliament building in an effort to block all exits and prevent MPs from leaving the premises. Police say the protests, which were declared as peaceful, quickly escalated and turned violent, announcing that three police officers were injured. Authorities say some protesters threw firecrackers and glass bottles at deployed officers and attempted to overturn a police van. The protest came ahead of a final parliamentary vote to gain approval and just a few weeks before the Balkan nation is set to enter the Eurozone.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: The Global South's mineral wealth, a game changer for economic growth, but at what cost? The G20's 2025 Summit in Johannesburg, South Africa has ignited a crucial conversation about the role of critical minerals in shaping our future. But here's where it gets controversial. Can these resources truly drive inclusive growth and resilience, or will they perpetuate existing inequalities? In a bold move, the G20 has unveiled its critical minerals framework, aiming to transform these essential resources into catalysts for sustainable development. The plan? To empower mineral rich nations, particularly in the Global South, to move beyond simply exporting raw materials. And this is the part most people miss. The framework seeks to address the systemic challenges these countries face, from underinvestment and limited technology to socio-economic and environmental hurdles. As the world undergoes rapid economic transformations, think sustainable energy transitions, digitalization, and industrial innovation, the demand for critical minerals is skyrocketing. However, the G20 declaration highlights a stark reality. Many producer countries, especially developing nations, are struggling to capitalize on this opportunity. The framework offers a voluntary, non-binding road map to foster sustainable, transparent, and resilient mineral value chains. This includes boosting investment in exploration, promoting local processing, beneficiation, and strengthening governance for responsible mining practices. Here's the catch. While the framework promises to preserve the sovereign rights of mineral rich countries, it also raises questions about equitable benefit sharing and environmental stewardship. Will local communities truly reap the rewards or will multinational corporations dominate the landscape. The G20 encourages collaboration among governments, private sectors, investors, and local communities, but how will this play out in practice? Prime Minister Narendra Modi emphasized the importance of international cooperation in addressing global challenges from climate change to food systems. India's commitment to a human-centric, sustainable, and inclusive future aligns with the G20's vision. But as the summit concludes, one question lingers, can critical minerals truly become a force for broad-based development, or will they remain a source of raw material exports leaving the global south behind? Let's spark a conversation that could shape the future of global resource management.

answer: Most worlds end once, but this one has died and returned more times than anyone can count. Every time the snow melts, the servers close, and then somehow someone brings it all back. We built versions of who we hoped to be. The confident one in red, the quiet one in blue, the dreamer, the explorer, the one who finally fit in. We were shaping identity before we even knew the word for it. There is a psychological theory called the Proteus effect. It says when you change your avatar, your behavior changes with it. Maybe that's why the shy kids led the conga lines here. Maybe that's why the lonely ones hosted parties every night. It was safer to be bold when you were just made of pixels. In here, we could be someone else. And sometimes, that's the truest version of who we are. Every snowball was a conversation, every emote was a way of saying I see you in a language that nobody taught us. Connection didn't need a voice chat, just timing, intention, a small gesture across the screen. We were learning empathy without knowing its name. The dojo was the only place where stillness felt like progress. No coins, no leaderboards, just patience. For once, the goal wasn't just to win, it was to understand a rhythm and yourself. It's 2025, and somehow we are here again. Different people, same avatars. The penguins grew up, but they returned anyway. Maybe because this world never judged us for who we were or who we were trying to become. Every home we built here was a fragment of comfort. We arranged these rooms like we arranged our hearts, cluttered, colorful, and desperately personal. There's something tender about rebuilding a world no one asked you to bring back. Club Penguin Zero isn't about nostalgia. It's about proof that versions of ourselves we once loved still exist somewhere, waiting under the snow. We return to remember. We stay to rebuild. question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Curious commuters recently noticed a massive vault-like door near Exit 5 of Taipei Metro's Nanjing Fushing Station, sparking online speculation about its purpose. Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation clarified that the heavy, sealed structure is a flood barrier system, a vital defense mechanism designed after the devastating floods caused by Typhoon Nari in 2001. During that storm, floodwaters inundated the Blue Bannan Line and even swamped Taipei Main Station, reaching depths of up to 2.3 m. The disaster led Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation to design and install multiple waterproof systems across the network. If flooding threatens, this watertight door, 30 cm thick, can be closed to prevent water from entering the platform level, said CTS reporter Chang Hsiaoyun, while demonstrating the mechanism on site. According to Huang Yi Chao, a section chief from the Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit systems, the doors were introduced after engineers realized that flooding could easily overwhelm stations entrances. We decided to place basic waterproofing at the entrances and add full seal floodgates at station interfaces, he explained. The Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation uses several types of flood barriers, including swinging, vertical, and sliding models, to block water from penetrating underground areas. Although forecasts predict less rain from this week's Typhoon Fung Wong than from Nari, with expected totals around 300 mm over 2 days, city officials said the metro system remains on high alert to ensure uninterrupted service. Filip Stawski for ICRT News.

question: Describe the audio content in detail.

This video provides an educational overview of the AIDAAS model, a structured framework for effective communication. The presenter guides the listener through each of the five stages: Attention (capturing your audience's focus), Interest (sparking curiosity with relevant information), Desire (creating a want for your offering), Action (prompting a specific next step with a clear call to action), and Satisfaction (ensuring long-term happiness and building relationships). The tutorial offers practical tips for each phase, encourages practice through exercises, and concludes by prompting reflection on the ethical application of this powerful communication tool.

Welcome. Today we delve into the AIDAAS model, a powerful tool to elevate your communication. The AIDAAS model is a structured approach that guides your audience through the journey of communication. Are you ready to learn the secrets of successful communication? Let's get started.

Attention is the first crucial step. You need to capture your audience's attention immediately. In a world of information overload, a structured approach is key to making your message stand out. Use powerful headlines, striking images, and focus on the benefit for your audience to grab attention.

Once you have attention, you must spark interest. This is where you engage your audience further. Reveal the hook by making your message relevant to your audience. This is about you. Engage interest with facts, relatable stories, and highlight how your product or idea solves their problem.

Now, transform interest into desire. Your audience should want what you're offering. Your goal is to form the 'I want it' response. Make them feel a strong desire for your offering. Connect emotionally, visualize the outcome, show social proof, and use restrictions to drive desire.

The action stage is about getting your audience to take the desired next step. Provide a clear call to action (CTA). Tell them exactly what you want them to do. Make taking action as simple as possible. Remove any obstacles that might stop them.

Satisfaction is about ensuring your audience is happy. After the action is taken, turn a client into a fan by building long-term relationships. Go beyond the sale to ensure their satisfaction. Provide excellent support, service, and ensure you fulfill your promise to solidify satisfaction.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: How did journalists cover the Berlin Wall's construction? Imagine waking up to a city suddenly divided overnight. That's exactly what happened on August 13, 1961, when the Berlin Wall began to rise. Journalists were quick to report this startling change, capturing the shock and confusion felt by Berliners. News outlets described how barbed wire and barricades appeared suddenly, cutting East Berlin off from West Berlin. Reporters used vivid words like barbed wire, steel barriers, and military presence to paint a picture of the tense scene. Radio stations, especially from the American sector, played a vital role. Stations like Radio in the American Sector provided live updates, warning people about the new restrictions and urging caution. Journalists on the ground described soldiers reinforcing the wall with steel barriers and East German troops patrolling the border. Newspapers in the West published eyewitness accounts, emphasizing how families were separated and freedoms restricted. They highlighted the speed of construction and the human toll of this sudden division. West Berlin's leaders, including the mayor, expressed outrage and called for support from Western allies. These statements were widely covered, showing the political tension. The East German government initially denied plans to build a wall, with leaders like Walter Ulbricht claiming there was no intention to do so. As the wall went up, journalists reported on this contradiction, illustrating the propaganda battles happening alongside the physical construction. International coverage also focused on the broader Cold War tensions. Reports described US troop movements and the famous tank confrontation at Checkpoint Charlie later that year. Journalists framed the wall as a symbol of communist oppression and the deep ideological divide between East and West. During the 1960s, coverage was full of urgency and emotion. Reporters told stories of fear, hope, and resilience of Berliners living through one of the Cold War's most defining moments. They combined eyewitness accounts with political analysis, capturing the era's style of reporting. This coverage helped the world understand the significance of the Berlin Wall's construction and its impact on global politics.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: There are many ways to build a quantum computer. Each uses qubits, quantum bits, as its core building block. But no matter the method, all qubits, whether superconducting qubits, trapped ions, neutral atoms or photons, share the same challenge. They're fragile and extremely sensitive to noise. Today's qubits remain stable for only a few hundred operations, but solving meaningful problems requires trillions of operations. The answer is quantum error correction. Measuring disturbs a qubit, which destroys the information inside it. The trick is to add extra qubits, entangled, so that measuring them gives us enough information to calculate where errors occurred without damaging the qubits we care about. It's brilliant, but needs beyond state-of-the-art conventional compute. That's why we built NVQLink, a new interconnect architecture that directly connects quantum processors with Nvidia GPUs. Quantum error correction requires reading out information from qubits, calculating where errors occur, and sending data back to correct them. NVQLink is capable of moving terabytes of data to and from quantum hardware, the thousands of times every second needed for quantum error correction. At its heart is CUDA-Q, our open platform for quantum GPU computing. Using NVQLink and CUDA-Q, researchers will be able to do more than just error correction. They will also be able to orchestrate quantum devices and AI supercomputers to run quantum GPU applications. Quantum computing won't replace classical systems. They will work together, fused into one accelerated quantum supercomputing platform.

answer: I have with me right now the TCL NXT Paper 14 and the TCL NXT Paper 11 Plus. and over the past couple of months, I have been testing out these two tablets. So, I just wanted to give you guys my honest thoughts on them, see how they stack up against each other. And overall, give you guys just a few things to consider before you settle on one of the two. The first and most obvious difference between the two is obviously going to be the screen size. The 11 Plus is lighter, faster, and more portable. It's got an 11 and a half inch 2.2K display and runs on NXT Paper 4.0 technology. Not only that, but it also has a 120 Hz refresh rate, and that refresh rate is going to be super important, especially for someone that values a lot smoother and more seamless browsing experience. When you compare the two, the 11 Plus is smoother for navigation, animations, and stylus interactions, while the 14 is geared more towards reading, writing, and large format use. The 11 Plus comes with a stylus, supports pressure assist, and unlike the Paper 14, it comes with a few different AI features like text assist and writing assist. You're also getting an 8 GB RAM and 8 GB of virtual memory storage, as well as 256 GB of regular storage, which is on par with the Paper 14. One key difference with the 11 Plus is that it's getting a faster MediaTek G100 chip, all packed into a slim and lightweight body just under 500 grams. The battery sizes on the two tablets will differ slightly as well. The 11 Plus comes with an 8,000 mAh hour battery while the 14 comes with a 10,000 mAh hour battery. Honestly, although the 11 Plus did come with a smaller battery, I found that the difference in battery life with just normal practical use was pretty negligible. I typically got around two days of moderate use out of both tablets and well over a week of standby time. Now, if you're someone that values screen real estate a lot more, the NXT Paper 14 definitely delivers. This tablet has a huge 14.3-inch display, also comes with a 2.4K resolution. However, it only has a 60 Hz refresh rate. In terms of software, it's running NXT Paper 3.0, which focuses more on a paper-like and anti-glare look, and it's definitely perfect for sketching or reading. You still get the stylus with 4,096 pressure levels, plus a flip case and multi-window multitasking. Overall, I thought there was a lot more of a heavier emphasis on productivity and multitasking with the Paper 14 opposed to the 11 Plus. And that probably had to do with the bigger screen and the ability to switch through different tabs fairly easily. The 11 Plus was definitely meant to be a lot more portable and an easier alternative for students that didn't want to take around a bulky laptop to class. The key takeaways that I got from this experience is that the 11 Plus is more balanced for hybrid use. It offers a high refresh rate, a more advanced display generation, lighter weight, AI features, and a comfortable size for one-hand or mixed usage. On the other hand, the 14 is better suited if your priority is to have a larger canvas. It's really good for reading long documents, viewing diagrams, or large pages, multitasking, or using it more like an actual tablet or digital notebook. You'll ultimately be trading off portability and smoothness for a more immersive experience. All in all, I do think both tablets do have their pros and cons, and ultimately, it kind of just boils down to how you want to use it and how you envision it in your day-to-day life. All things considered, I definitely still recommend both tablets as really strong contenders against the competition.

answer: The quiet visitors. Not every comet is a headline grabber. Some slip through the solar system as faint smudges, their passage noted only by dedicated observers. Among the seven visitors of 2025, two fall into this quiet category. C 2022 E3 or Panstars, and the periodic comet, 240p NEET. C 2022 E3 reaches its perihelion on July 31st at a chilly distance of 3.82 astronomical units, or about 571 million kilometers from the sun. At that range, it's not expected to brighten beyond a modest magnitude 10, visible only in medium-sized telescopes. Then there's 240p NEET, which was discovered in 2002 and returns every 7.6 years. It makes its pass on December 19th at a distance of 2.12 astronomical units, or 317 million kilometers. Its performance will likely be even dimmer, a low key encore for those tracking its well-documented path. For both of these objects, the primary audience will be astronomers contributing data to the minor Planet Center, where every verified observation helps refine orbital calculations. Even these faint comets provide crucial data on things like nucleus rotation and the slow development of their comas. They are the workhorses of cometary science, providing a baseline of normal activity against which the brighter comets can be compared.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Imagine a city already reeking of plague, piled high with timber houses, and stuffed with gunpowder. Then picture one careless spark. That was London, 1666. A tinderbox waiting to explode. It all began in a tiny bakery on Pudding Lane. A spark caught, the flame spread, and within hours, London was an inferno. Roofs collapsed, fireballs lept across streets, and terrified families clawed through smoke trying to escape. The city's wooden homes burned like matchsticks, while the wind turned alleys into fire tunnels. People fled, carrying whatever they could, some clutching furniture, others dragging half-burnt livestock. Most with nothing but ash on their skin. The fire raged for four days. St. Paul's Cathedral, that proud symbol of London, crumbled in the flames. Warehouses full of oil, tar, and brandy exploded into firestorms. By the end, over 13,000 houses and 87 churches were reduced to charred rubble. And while the city burned, rumors spread like sparks. Foreigners were blamed, Catholics were accused of sabotage, innocents were lynched in the streets by mobs who thought the fire was a plot. But here's the real kicker. London wasn't just burning, it was already crawling with plague. The fire roared through neighborhoods where corpses still lay rotting in homes. Some whispered the flames were God's punishment, others that it was mercy, burning the pestilence out. In the chaos, law and order collapsed. Looters picked through burning ruins. Rioters murdered anyone they suspected of starting it. The city was a vision of hell where firelight made night look like blood red day. When the smoke finally cleared, 100,000 Londoners were homeless. Families slept in fields under the September rain. The city stank of ash, rot, and despair. Yet somehow, from the wreckage, London began to rebuild. Brick by brick, flameproof this time. The Great Fire didn't just destroy London. It reshaped it. It burned away the medieval heart of the city, replacing it with something new. But for those who watched their world turn to cinders, it was the apocalypse.

Lions are the only cats that live in large social groups called prides. A pride usually consists of related lionesses, their cubs, and a few dominant males. Life in the pride revolves around teamwork. The lionesses share responsibilities: nursing cubs, defending territory, and hunting for food.

Boston's Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority provides detailed maps of bus routes and the subway system, especially the red line that stops at Harvard Square. These transit maps help you plan your trip from Boston to Harvard easily. question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Can I take a self-guided tour of Harvard University? Imagine walking through one of the most famous college campuses in the world, all at your own pace. If that sounds exciting, you might wonder if you can explore Harvard University on your own. The good news is yes, you can take a self-guided tour of Harvard. The campus and the nearby Cambridge area are very welcoming to visitors who want to see the sights without a group. You can plan your own route to visit key spots like Harvard Yard, the historic center of the university, and the John Harvard statue, which is a popular photo spot. You can also check out Widener Library, a stunning building filled with millions of books, and Memorial Hall, a grand structure built to honor Harvard students who served in wars. Harvard Square, the lively neighborhood around the campus, is full of shops, cafes, and street performers, making it a fun place to explore on your own. To make your self-guided tour easier, Harvard offers downloadable maps and GPS-enabled audio guides. These guides give you background stories and facts about each landmark, so you learn as you walk. Harvard University is located in Cambridge, just across the Charles River from Boston, so it's easy to reach by public transit. The best way to start your tour is by taking the Red Line subway, called the T, to the Harvard Square station. Once there, you can begin your walk at popular spots like Out of Town Newsstand or the Harvard Square MBTA station. The typical self-guided tour covers about 1.4 miles and takes around 2 hours. This gives you plenty of time to see everything without rushing. If you want to spend more time at certain sites, you can easily do so. While self-guided tours do not include a live guide, the maps and audio guides provide enough information to make your visit interesting and educational. Harvard also offers guided tours led by students, which give more detailed stories and insights. But if you prefer exploring on your own, the self-guided option is a flexible and popular choice. From the perspective of the city of Boston, Harvard is a nearby cultural and educational landmark. It's a quick trip across the river, making it perfect for residents and visitors who want to experience a historic university on their own schedule. So, yes, you absolutely can take a self-guided tour of Harvard University and enjoy discovering its history and beauty at your own pace.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Let's talk about a man who looks at our world and thinks, not enough. I'm talking about Elon Musk. As of today, August 29th, 2025, he is the wealthiest person on our planet with a fortune built on electric cars, solar panels, and of course, rockets. But Musk isn't just collecting billions of dollars to build bigger houses or own more companies. He has a much grander, some would say much stranger goal. He wants to die on Mars. Not from a crash landing, mind you, but of old age as a resident of a new human civilization on the red planet. This isn't just a casual wish. It is the central driving force behind his life's work and the ultimate destination for his vast fortune. Why Mars? Why pour hundreds of billions of dollars into a project that many see as pure science fiction? For Musk, the answer is simple and profound. Survival. He views humanity as living in a single fragile basket. Earth is that basket. A catastrophic event, a massive asteroid impact, a super volcano, or even a self-inflicted disaster like a global war, could wipe us out completely. To ensure the long-term survival of human consciousness and our species, he argues, we must become multi-planetary. It's a form of cosmic life insurance. He has even pointed to the eventual expansion of our own sun, which will one day make Earth uninhabitable, framing this mission with an almost biblical sense of urgency. This motivation goes beyond just a backup plan. There's a philosophical and perhaps even a political layer to his ambition. For years, Musk presented Mars as a new frontier, a blank slate where humanity could start over, free from the old problems of Earth. It was a vision of a libertarian paradise among the stars. However, recent reports, particularly from his old colleague, Peter Thiel, suggest a shift in his thinking. The fear that a woke AI or a sprawling Earth-based government could simply follow humanity to Mars, has apparently tempered his view of the red planet as a political escape hatch, complicating his once clear-cut futuristic narrative. This grand vision isn't just talk. Musk has dedicated his wealth, estimated at over 335 billion dollars earlier this year, to making this happen. He has repeatedly stated that the entire purpose of accumulating his fortune is to fund the colonization of Mars. This makes him a unique figure in the history of wealth. While other billionaires have focused on philanthropy here on Earth, Musk's philanthropic project is on a planetary scale. He is the modern equivalent of a Pharaoh building a pyramid, not as a tomb, but as a launch pad to a new world. His companies, SpaceX and Tesla, are the tools he is forging for this monumental task.

answer: About a quarter acre of heavy brush burned uphill near the 2,100 block of North Sunset Plaza Drive, threatening several homes above the fire. The Los Angeles Fire Department dispatched roughly 80 personnel, supported by helicopters and hand crews. Aerial water drops significantly slowed the blaze's advance toward residences. Initial reports indicated a vehicle fire that spread into medium heavy brush toward a hillside home. Mutual aid air and ground units from LA County Fire also responded. By evening, crews had extinguished all active flames and stopped the fire's forward progress. Helicopters continued water drops between homes to cool hotspots, while hand crews worked uphill on steep terrain aiming for full containment. Ground crews prioritized structure defense for the at-risk houses. Authorities issued shelter in place orders for Genesis zones LFDO817, LFDO819 and LFDO911. No civilian injuries were reported. Separately that morning, a two-story house on the 10,300 block of North Christine Place in Chatsworth caught fire after flames were observed on the first floor and spreading toward the rear. About 37 firefighters initiated an immediate offensive. The blaze was reported knocked down by 11:39 a.m. with around 53 personnel handling suppression, overhaul and scene stabilization. All occupants were evacuated and accounted for. One firefighter suffered a minor burn and was treated at the scene. City departments collaborated on the incident. The Department of Water and Power handled utilities, transportation managed traffic disruptions and building and safety conducted structural assessments. Motorists were urged to seek alternate routes due to congestion. Officials credited rapid multi-agency response, aggressive firefighting and aerial support with preventing greater property loss and injuries. Crews remained on scene working hotspots and containment.

Just imagine, riders won't need to wear helmets or protective jackets anymore. The secret lies in the inherent safety structure at the heart of its design. An idea that BMW actually tried more than 25 years ago.
Its history began in 2000 with the BMW C1, a unique scooter featuring a roof, roll cage, and seatbelt. Although not mass-produced, the C1 has a loyal following who prioritize comfort over the classic scooter style. Two decades later, BMW succeeded with the CE04 and CE02, two electric scooters that proved eco-friendly mobility can still be stylish. Now, Vision CE brings the C1 legacy, but in a modern format with proven electric technology. The most striking feature of the Vision CE is the safety cell. A metal alloy tube frame with custom seats and seatbelts. This system is designed to provide protection like a small car cabin, so helmets are no longer mandatory. This approach could be a solution to two major obstacles for two-wheeled commuters, the hassle of wearing gear and feeling hot in warm weather. From a design perspective, the Vision CE appears long, low, and futuristic. The safety frame is lightweight and open, more like an architectural framework than a cage. The chosen colors are simple yet elegant. Matte white combined with black, with neon red accents that give a modern and technical feel. The exposed aluminum details add a sense of robustness, while the matte seats and fine lettering keep the look minimalist. Another interesting feature is the self-balancing technology, which keeps the scooter upright even when stopped. Practical at red lights, easy for beginners, and provides a greater sense of stability. Technically, the Vision CE is based on the BMW CE04, which has 42 horsepower and a range of up to 130 km. Indeed, adding a safety frame can increase weight and slightly reduce performance, but BMW emphasizes that this scooter is specifically designed for short-distance urban travel. Although it's still a concept, BMW is known for often bringing ideas from the Vision CE into production. If it's truly marketed, the production version will likely add an aerodynamic roof for weather protection while also reinforcing the helmet-free claim. This combination of safety, comfort, and efficiency has the potential to attract more city commuters, even those who were previously reluctant to ride motorcycles due to inconvenience or risk.

answer:
Where was Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon filmed?
Have you ever wondered where the breathtaking scenes of Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon were captured? This iconic film, directed by Ang Lee, is a beautiful representation of Chinese culture and cinema. It takes us back to early 19th-century imperial China, showcasing stunning landscapes and intricate artistry.
The film was primarily shot in China, utilizing a mix of natural beauty and elaborate sets. One of the most notable locations is the Huangshan region in Anhui province. This area is famous for its dramatic granite peaks and lush pine forests, creating a striking backdrop for many scenes. The unique scenery adds depth to the film, making it visually captivating.
Another key filming site is the Anji Bamboo Forest in Zhejiang province. This serene forest is known for its lush bamboo groves, providing a tranquil environment that perfectly complements the film's more peaceful moments. The beauty of this location truly enhances the film's aesthetic.
Beijing, the capital city of China, also played a role in the filming process. The urban landscape of Beijing contributed to the cultural aspects of the story, showcasing the blend of tradition and modernity in Chinese life.
Chengde, located in Hebei province, was another filming location. This city offers a mix of historical and natural settings, which helped to create the film's rich visual narrative. The combination of these diverse locations allowed the filmmakers to capture the essence of Chinese culture.
Additionally, Hengdian World Studios in Zhejiang province was utilized for creating elaborate sets. As the largest film studio in the world, it provided the facilities needed to recreate traditional Chinese architecture and settings. This studio played a vital role in bringing the film's story to life.
Together, these locations contributed to the film's success, highlighting China's rich cultural heritage and stunning natural beauty. Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon is not just a film. It is a celebration of Chinese arts and performing arts, making it a significant part of Chinese cinema history. Each location, from the majestic mountains to the serene bamboo forests, adds to the film's enchanting narrative, leaving a lasting impression on audiences worldwide.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: In the world of smartphones, there's slim, and then there's Apple slim. This year, the tech giant is reportedly preparing to unveil its thinnest iPhone ever, the iPhone 17 Air, a device so slender it could almost vanish into your pocket at just 5.5 mm thick. It's a bold statement in design, a featherweight champion in the palm of your hand. But here's the catch, making a phone this thin often comes with a price. And according to reliable leaks, Apple may be trimming more than just the edges. At the heart of the iPhone 17 Air lies a special version of Apple's latest A19 Pro chip, the same powerhouse expected in the Pro and Pro Max models. Almost. The difference? One less GPU core. That might seem small, and for everyday scrolling, streaming, or texting, you probably won't notice. But push it with 3D gaming or heavy video editing, and the performance gap could become clear. Then there's the heat factor. A thinner body means less space to dissipate heat, increasing the chance of thermal throttling, where your phone slows down to cool off during extended workloads. And of course, a slimmer frame means a smaller battery. Translation, bursts of power, but maybe not the all-day stamina many users demand. The compromises don't stop there. To keep the air ultra thin, Apple is rumored to strip it down to a single rear camera, skip the high refresh rate display, and possibly reduce speaker output to just one channel. It's a list of sacrifices that make the Pro models, or even rival Androids, look more versatile by comparison. And yet, there's an audience for this. People who value elegance over excess. For them, the iPhone 17 Air could be the ultimate expression of Apple's design philosophy, light, minimal, and effortlessly stylish. Still, the question remains, will consumers trade performance, battery life, and features for a sleeker silhouette? When it launches, the iPhone 17 Air won't just be another smartphone. answer: Hey, it's Kevin, and this is my recap of the To-Do list summit in San Francisco this past weekend. And content is the most affordable and efficient way to provide that value first. And the third one is that consistency is key, but only if the content is consistently high quality. answer:
What birds can you see in the Masai Mara?
Have you ever wondered what birds you might encounter in the stunning Masai Mara? This incredible region in Kenya is a paradise for bird lovers, boasting over 580 recorded species. The variety of habitats here, from open savanna to wetlands, supports an amazing range of birds. Let's start with the impressive birds of prey. The Masai Mara is home to many eagle species. You might spot the Tawny Eagle, Steppe Eagle, and Imperial Eagle soaring above. Other raptors include the African Hawk-Eagle and Verreaux's Eagle. If you keep your eyes peeled, you may also see the Bat Hawk and several types of buzzards like the Common Buzzard and Long-legged Buzzard. As you wander through the grasslands, look out for the large ground birds. The Common Ostrich is a prominent sight, strutting across the savanna. Near the rivers and wetlands, you can find various waterfowl. Keep an eye out for the White-faced Whistling Duck and the Northern Pintail among others. Wading birds are also abundant in the Masai Mara. Plover and lapwing species are often seen near water bodies. You might encounter the Little Ringed Plover and the Kittlitz's Plover. The Blacksmith Lapwing and the Spur-winged Lapwing are also common in these areas. In the wetlands, look for the Greater Painted-snipe and the African Jacana. These birds thrive in the lush environments created by the rivers and marshes. The diversity of birds here reflects the rich ecological variety of the Masai Mara. The different habitats, including riverine forests and acacia woodlands, provide food and nesting sites for many species. This makes the Masai Mara a vital area for bird survival and reproduction. The presence of various raptors indicates a healthy ecosystem with plenty of prey. For birdwatchers, the Masai Mara offers a unique opportunity to see a wide range of African birdlife in one location. Whether you are a seasoned birder or just starting, this region is a must-visit for anyone interested in birds. With its rich diversity and stunning scenery, the Masai Mara truly is a birding hotspot in Kenya.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: After four days of festivities, the World Eskimo Indian Olympics are wrapping up in Fairbanks. This year's event saw world records broken, a crowd a crown passed, and a community gathered to celebrate indigenous culture. Adrian Peterson and Alex Bengal were there today and give us a roundup of the week. The fourth and final day of the 64th annual WEO has arrived. Here at the Carlson Center in Fairbanks, this year's WEO games featured more than 20 competitive events from the four-man carry to the bench reach. Sportsmanship and camaraderie were displayed throughout the games as athletes faced difficult feats. Honestly, I think one foot and two foot are the most challenging if I'm going to be honest. I feel like you know, jumping and then kicking the ball is was a lot for me. Despite the strain and skill testing tasks, newcomers and veteran athletes alike found success during the games with one athlete beating his very own world record on the first day. You just got to have the confidence. Confidence, put the consistency in your practices. Oh, definitely work out a lot and you know, you're you're confident because how are you going to perform if you put in all the work? But the event was about more than sports. It was a chance for the community to get together and for people from around the state and the world to share their culture. Regalia contests with contestants ages 6 months and up showed off unique and elaborate use of hide and cloth. Regalia is really our way to be able to honor our the animals who allowed us to um hunt them. And then also our family, because like I said, it's a family effort. A lot of the patterns are specific to families. Throughout the games, the arena was filled with tables for people to display and sell handmade arts and crafts, made with love and care from all kinds of materials. It's also really healing for your soul, like just sitting there and just healing with your ancestors who were there before you. And a new Miss Wio was crowned Friday night, Jolie Carlson from Bethel and Quetlook. We're still here. We still have our cultures, we still have our traditions, we still have our languages, we know who we are. And it's all still intact and it will be for generations to come. A community gathering to keep culture alive and to pass their knowledge and skills on to the next generation. Adrian Peterson and Alex Bengal, Alaska's News Source.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: At first glance, this looks like your average gas station on a quiet corner in Kansas City. But step inside and you'll find ribs, brisket, and a barbecue sandwich so legendary, it once made Anthony Bourdain's list of places to eat before you die. It all started with a man named Jeff Steny. Just a regular guy with a serious love for barbecue. In the early 1990s, he and his wife Joy began competing in barbecue contests around the country, under the name Slaughterhouse 5. They didn't just enter competitions, they dominated them. In 1993, they won the Grand Championship at the American Royal, the Super Bowl of barbecue. With their reputation growing, the Steny's decided to open a restaurant. But instead of some flashy new building, they picked something unexpected. A working gas station at 47th and Mission. Yes, they literally served brisket next to gas pumps. No frills, no fancy, just honest, slow-smoked barbecue. Orders started flying in. And in 2009, food legend Anthony Bourdain called Joe's one of the 13 places to eat before you die. What made it so special? Maybe it's the slow-smoked meats. Maybe it's the Z-Man sandwich, tender brisket topped with onion rings and provolone. Or maybe, it's the story. Joe's isn't just a restaurant. It's a reminder that greatness can come from the humblest places. That passion, patience, and a whole lot of smoke can turn a gas station into a bucket list destination. If you go, head to the original location, 47th and Mission. Get there early, lines form fast. Locals swear by the Z-Man and the burnt ends. And yes, it's worth the wait. Joe's Kansas City barbecue began with a dream and a smoker in a gas station. And it became one of the most legendary barbecue joints in America. Because sometimes, the best places are the ones you'd never expect.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: The London Marathon from pure race to brand playground. Once upon a time, the London Marathon was a straightforward celebration of running. Thousands of runners shared a goal and a spirit for the sport. But fast forward to 2025, it's a whole different marathon. A stage where brands flex their creative muscles as much as the runners do theirs. Take New Balance, for example. They didn't just sponsor the marathon, they created an entire townhouse near Regent Street. Runners could customize their gear, attend motivational talks, and feel like part of an exclusive community. However, not all brand activations hit the mark this year. Nike's never again until next year billboard campaign intended to resonate with runners. Their sentiment post-marathon sparked significant controversy. The phrase never again is deeply associated with the Holocaust remembrance, and its use in this context was seen by many as trivializing a solemn vow. Nike issued an apology, stating that the intent was to motivate runners based on common phrases used in the world of running, but acknowledged the oversight and removed the billboards. This incident underscores the fine lines brands walk when integrating into cultural events. It raises the question, has all this branding overshadowed the essence of the marathon? There's no denying that today's races are as much about social media moments and brand storytelling as they are about the run itself. Every corner turned is another Instagrammable moment. Every mile marker is a brand opportunity, adding to the tapestry of brand engagements. Pure sport, for example, introduced a unique hotel room service. In the days leading up to the marathon, they offered a surprise delivery service to runners staying in London hotels. Participants who signed up via Pure Sports Instagram received recovery kits delivered directly to their rooms. These kits included hydration sachets, magnesium supplements, and marathon socks, essentials designed to aid performance and recovery. Yet, there is a flip side. These brand activations bring fresh eyes to the sport. They attract new runners and allow brands to push creative boundaries. The marathon is no longer just a race. It is a bit of a cultural phenomenon that merges sport, creativity, and community. And in the end, the London Marathon 2025 is a reflection of our times. It's not just about crossing the finish line, but also about the stories told along the way. And perhaps that's not such a bad thing after all. I'd be keen to hear your point of view on this. Do you feel that it is a big brand opportunity to spend some cash and make moves? Or is it for the reasons greater than that? Please do drop your comments below, and don't forget to like and subscribe for more stories into the world of sport and culture surrounding us.

Welcome to Osaka, Japan's vibrant city of food, culture, and unforgettable experiences. Let's explore the top tourist attractions you can't miss in this amazing destination.

First up, Dotonbori, Osaka's entertainment hotspot. Famous for its glowing neon lights, street food, and bustling energy. It's the perfect place to taste takoyaki and soak in the city's nightlife.

For thrill-seekers and movie lovers, Universal Studios Japan is a must-visit. From Hogwarts to Mario Kart, it's a magical adventure for all ages.

One of the largest aquariums in the world, Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan lets you walk through a stunning underwater world featuring marine creatures from across the Pacific Ocean.

Step back in time at Osaka Castle, a historic icon of Japan. Surrounded by cherry blossoms in spring, it's a beautiful blend of power and peace.

Fashion lovers, this is your paradise. Shinsaibashi-suji offers a mix of modern boutiques, traditional shops, and endless options for every style.

Take a break in Osaka Castle Park. A tranquil escape with scenic views, perfect for a picnic or peaceful stroll around nature and history.

Enjoy breathtaking views from the Kuchu Teien Observatory atop the Umeda Sky Building. See all of Osaka from the sky, especially magical at sunset.

Feeling hungry? Head to Kuromon Market, also known as Osaka's kitchen, where you'll find fresh local food, sushi, and street snacks that'll make your mouth water.

Discover the spiritual side of Osaka at Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine, one of Japan's oldest Shinto shrines, known for its iconic bridge and peaceful atmosphere.

Minami, also known as Namba, is Osaka's beating heart, full of energy, fashion, food, and fun. It's where tradition meets modern life.

An architectural wonder, the Umeda Sky Building is not just for the views. It's also a great spot for photos, dining, and seeing the city sparkle at night.

answer: Paul McCartney may be preparing to return to the stage in the United States, with subtle hints suggesting that another leg of his Got Back tour could be on the horizon, possibly beginning as early as this year. On July 9, McCartney sparked speculation with an Instagram story that featured an intriguing image, two guitar picks, one white and one blue. The white pick had his name printed in red lettering, while the blue one read Got Back in 2025 in white text. Alongside the image, he included a link directing fans to a sign-up page on his official website. That web page encouraged visitors to register in order to receive updates about upcoming tour dates, ticket pre-sales, and other related announcements. The post has led many to believe that McCartney is teasing new US tour dates in 2025, signaling a possible continuation of his highly successful Got Back tour. Originally launched in April 2022, the Got Back tour began in Spokane, Washington, and saw McCartney performing across 16 American cities before concluding the US leg in June that same year. He then brought the show to fans in South America and Australia, eventually wrapping things up with a final European stretch. The tour concluded in December 2024 with two grand performances at London's O2 Arena. Concertgoers were treated to a vibrant mix of songs from across McCartney's career, including Beatles classics such as Can't Buy Me Love, Hey Jude, and Let It Be, as well as hits from his Wings era like Band on the Run, and beloved solo tracks including Maybe I'm Amazed. At 83, McCartney continues to command the stage with the same energy and charisma that made him a household name decades ago. The Got Back tour sold over 1 million tickets and reportedly earned close to 200 million in revenue, evidence that his appeal remains as strong as ever. With these latest clues, it appears that the legendary musician may be gearing up for yet another memorable tour across the US, much to the excitement of fans nationwide.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Back in the early 2000s, Capcom dropped Metal Walker onto the Game Boy Color and I gotta admit, I thought I had stumbled on some hidden mecha brawler gem. With a name like Metal Walker, you expect something gritty and full of robotic smackdowns, right? Well, you do get robots, but it's more like a Pokemon and a game of pool had a weird random baby. So here's the setup. You play as a kid looking for your dad on an island filled with relics from a mysterious metal called core. As you travel the island, you'll have a companion Metal Walker who's your little battle bot buddy that levels up and evolves based on core units. There are three types, land, marine, and sky. You can switch out orbs to give your bot new abilities. Some will let you smash rocks, one will let you cross water, and each one has different stats to tweak your strategy. Cool in theory, right? Now, the combat is where this game gets totally bonkers. It plays out on a top-down battlefield where instead of picking attacks from a menu, you'll launch your metal walker into enemies billiard style. You'll bounce off walls, collide with opponents, trigger environmental hazards, and hope RNG Jesus is on your side. Each round, a handful of random items spawn on the field, some helpful, some annoying, and by the way, enemies can pick them up too. So it can get chaotic pretty fast. Lining up a good shot is harder than you think, especially with the physics not quite behaving the way you would want it to. Add in the relentless encounter rate and you end up in constant fights that feel more like a chore than a challenge. I found myself wishing I could just turn it down a notch just so I can explore for more than 10 seconds. Speaking of exploration, this isn't a game where you can get lost. The NPCs give clear instructions on how to progress and the descriptions of places are pretty spot on. There's a neat mechanic where you can analyze enemies mid-battle to get new parts, which is probably the closest thing this game has to catching Pokémon. I ended up using a GameFAQs guide because some of the fights were getting too punishing without a bit of extra help. And trust me, the guide made a big difference. There are cheats available if you have a Game Genie or Game Shark. I didn't use any because I really do enjoy leveling up. Visually, Metal Walker is clean for a Game Boy Color title. The sprites are pretty sharp, and it all fits the sci-fi theme. The music was surprisingly great with a large soundtrack you won't get bored with. After all this praise, is it worth it? Honestly, no. The battle system is unique enough to keep me intrigued, but it's not the mecha brawler I expected. So, unless you're a collector or just dying for a fresh take on RPGs, you're better off watching a video or just reading about it.

The review highlights the game's pros, such as its clean sprites and "surprisingly great" music, but heavily criticizes the chaotic, RNG-dependent battles, frustrating physics, and a "relentless encounter rate" that makes the game feel like a chore. This tutorial provides a step-by-step guide on how to fix Nintendo Switch Joy-Con controllers that are not connecting, pairing, or charging properly. The video outlines a series of troubleshooting methods:

1.  **Power Off the Joy-Cons:** First, disconnect the Joy-Cons from the Switch and press the small circular sync button on the rail of each controller to turn it off. The LED lights should extinguish.

2.  **Update the Switch System:** Go to System Settings on your Switch, scroll down to 'System,' and select 'System Update' to ensure your console's software is current.

3.  **Power Cycle the Switch:** Perform a hard reset by holding down the power button on the console for about 20 seconds, ignoring the on-screen power menu, until the screen turns completely black. Then, power the Switch back on.

4.  **Reconnect and Update Controllers:** Attach the Joy-Cons back to the sides of the Switch. Navigate to System Settings > Controllers and Accessories, and select 'Update Controllers' to install the latest firmware for them.

5.  **Re-sync the Controllers:** If the issue continues, go to the 'Controllers' icon on the home screen, select 'Change Grip/Order,' and then press the sync button on each Joy-Con individually. A green LED light indicates a successful sync. Reattach the controllers to the Switch.

Following these steps should resolve most connection issues with your Joy-Con controllers.

One of those that I think that we'll see AI used a lot more in is areas of diagnostic support. I think what AI is really amazing at is taking a huge amount of context and information and finding key insights, condensing it down, and narrowing down this, you know, potential plethora of conditions that someone may have and finding the key points that will really point to like the root cause diagnosis for an individual. And I think that humans are very good at this too and it's actually very, very difficult to do. But I think that AI has, number one, the ability to ingest stupidly large amounts of context. So while me as a human doctor might need to read a summary of a patient that another doctor has written, it can actually end up, um an AI is able to ingest maybe 20 years of medical context about someone all at once. And so I'm very bullish on AI actually helping with areas such as diagnosis. And I'm actually very bullish on AI getting very strong in this area of diagnosis. That being said, I think there are areas that people thought AI would be amazing in, but haven't seen as much progress as we would have expected. A common one is everyone thought radiologists were going to be out of business. And so radiologists, um, are the people who will look at x-rays, MRIs, and scans and images and make conclusions or diagnosis from those images. And it seems like something an AI model should be really, really great at doing, but when people actually tried this out and implemented it, it's actually quite complex to do and there's a lot of moving parts. It's very difficult to train models on it. So it's very interesting seeing what's happened over the last 5 10 years because realistically, everyone's been screaming about AI in medicine for quite a while. answer: So what we discovered was that uh two species, the resident killer whales and Pacific white-sided dolphins seem to be cooperatively foraging on uh salmon, and most likely adult chinook salmon off the coast of BC. So we think this is important for a couple of reasons. The first is that interspecies interactions are commonly observed um around the world. So we see whales and dolphins or different species of whales that interact with one another. But understanding the actual mechanism or the reason why we're seeing both species interacting has largely been speculative. And that's because a lot of the behaviors that are occurring are underwater and we just can't see what's going on. But then once we put the suction cup tags on the whales that had cameras and acoustic recorders, then we could actually see that not only were the killer whales following dolphins at the surface, but they would follow them to depth, down to around 60 m, where it would become really dark and we could just see the silhouettes of the dolphins at the head of the whale. And so what this told us was that the whales are, you know, working together to target uh large salmon for the killer whales to capture. It's important because if there's maybe another mechanism or a way to help facilitate um the resident killer whales to find their food, then that might be advantageous for the population. But we need to collect more data to try to figure out like, is this really prevalent? Like, how often are resident killer whales cooperatively foraging with Pacific white-sided dolphins? And that's something that we've yet to determine. To see that things were perhaps a bit more complex than we initially understood is is always exciting because like we just, you know, you scratch the surface with a lot of the research that you do, and then every now and then you get kind of lucky and something unexpected happens. And so this is one of those kind of lucky things.

In this video, Alex from Meta Endurance provides a first look at the new Nike Structure Plus running shoe from the Nike booth at The Running Event (TRE) in San Antonio, Texas. question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: From demonstrating its rescue capabilities during disasters to busting a move and serving up drinks. The latest advances in humanoid robot technology are on full display at this year's International Robot Exhibition in Tokyo. The Kaleido 9 is using this toy cat to showcase how it could save people during a disaster. Yoshimoto Matsuda, managing executive officer of Kawasaki Heavy Industries, said the robot is meant to be deployed to disaster areas where access for humans is difficult. We aim to create robots that are robust and reliable for deployment in places where humans cannot work or where they need to work alongside robots. That's why we insist on human-sized robots, so existing equipment like fireproof suits and protective gear can be used without modification. Our vision is not about robots performing repetitive tasks in factories or improving precision, but about working on site, improvising, and using the same tools as humans. Kawasaki spent about a decade developing the robot, which is still in the testing phase. The bot showed off how it can be a lifesaver in other ways, including performing domestic duties like raking up leaves and throwing out the trash. Across the exhibition hall, a dance-off is taking place. This robot was manufactured by Chinese robotics developer Unitree, but programmed and calibrated by Japanese robotics company GMO. Tomohiro Uchida of GMO said the dance moves show just how far robotic development has come. About a year ago, humanoid robots were still very stiff and jerky. People couldn't imagine them functioning in real-world settings. But in the past six months, or even the last three months, the software has been rapidly updated. And now they can perform a variety of movements. So we wanted visitors to see what kind of movements are possible now. As part of that demonstration, we had it perform a dance. It appears to move quite fluidly now. Uchida added that he sees humanoid robots as a solution to help fill gaps in what he called a declining labor force in developed countries.

Welcome to your new ROG Xbox Ally. Getting started couldn't be easier.

When you first boot the device, you'll be greeted with a streamlined Windows setup. Follow the prompts to connect to Wi-Fi, log into your Microsoft account, and set up the fingerprint sensor on the power button. After that, you'll be dropped into the new Xbox full-screen experience, which puts your games front and center. But, before you start browsing, you might want to update all of your software. We've already released a number of improvements for day one users. So tap the bell icon in the Xbox app and download any updates it finds. Once that's done, press the command center button on the left side of the device and tap open Armory Crate SE. Inside the update center, you'll find a number of new updates that will add new features, improve performance, and more. Note that one of these will be a BIOS update, which requires you to plug your Ally into a power outlet. Make sure not to turn off the device while it updates. Once you've got the latest software, you're ready to start gaming. From the new Xbox app, you can check out new games in the store or dive right in with Xbox Game Pass. The ROG Ally comes with three months free, so you can start playing right away. To browse your games, press the library button on the right side of the device. You can download games to play them locally on your device, stream them from the cloud with a Game Pass subscription, or remote play from your Xbox console. The new aggregated library shows not just your Xbox games, but games from battle.net and other leading storefronts as well. So you can install any game you own on PC and start playing. Pressing the Xbox button will show your most recent games as well as your other game launchers, so you can easily find and install more titles. You can navigate the game bar with the left and right bumpers. Moving to the left will show you the Armory Crate command center where you can quick toggle different hardware settings. Put your Ally in silent mode for better battery life or crank it up to turbo mode for maximum performance. Launching Armory Crate SE will give you even more hardware options to play with, from vibration intensity to joystick sensitivity and even gyro controls. You can also press and hold the command center button to go directly to the gaming co-pilot tab, which can give you game recommendations, provide strategies for those tough bosses, or fill you in on an NPC. Or you can long press the library button to quickly start a conversation with gaming co-pilot without ever leaving your game. Finally, at any time you can press and hold the Xbox button or swipe up on the bottom of the screen to open the task switcher. From here you can see your open apps, flip between them, or open the Windows desktop where you can do anything that's possible on a Windows PC. The simplicity of Xbox meets the power of Windows.

Naturally, backup arrived in the form of Sheamus and Rey Mysterio, and suddenly, we had a six-man tag team match. At first, I thought it was a bit odd to go six-man instead of a one-on-one moment for Cena's farewell, but by the end, it worked perfectly. It was the kind of feel good story WWE does best. Good guys win, Cena hits every signature move, and you could see him having a blast with the other veterans. The crowd loved every second of it. Raw overall delivered after that. We saw the return of Dolph Ziggler, Roman Reigns and Brock Lesnar joining the men's War Games match in an intense main event brawl segment. AJ Lee made a shocking impact by costing Becky Lynch the women's Intercontinental Championship and Gunther had a standout match with Giovanni Evans. WWE treated Cena's farewell like the special occasion it was, and the entire show felt elevated. Rumors are already swirling that John Cena will headline the 2026 WWE Hall of Fame class, which makes you wonder if he was offered that honor backstage last night. Vince McMahon might not have been the right choice to induct him given his history, but who steps up now? Triple H is likely inducting Stephanie McMahon, so he's probably out. Could it be Randy Orton, CM Punk, or maybe a veteran legend like Kurt Angle or the Undertaker? Whatever happens, it'll be historic. Madison Square Garden provided the perfect backdrop for a proper farewell. Cena's energy, the crowd's love, and the celebration with his peers reminded everyone why he's one of the most iconic performers in WWE history. That night wasn't just about a goodbye, it was a celebration of a career that shaped an entire generation. And while the Hall of Fame speculation adds intrigue, last night was about one thing. Honoring Cena, the man, the performer, the legend. Fans got to witness a truly memorable Raw, and WWE delivered a show that will be talked about for years. Shout out to Netflix for giving us front row access to the magic.

answer: We just got our clearest look yet at DJI's next ultra light drone, and it's not just a refresh. If you thought the mini series had peaked, you might want to sit down for this. The leak front-facing shot instantly gives away a few big upgrades. Front and center, a redesigned gimbal housing a one-inch camera sensor. Between the two main lenses, LAR sensors, an addition that hints at smarter obstacle avoidance. Even the motors have been updated, darker in color, but more importantly, compatible with quick release propellers for faster swaps in the field. Flip it over and the changes keep coming. For the first time in a mini series drone, there's a power lead port, just like the Mavic and Air lines. But the real head turner, it's expected to carry a C0 classification, keeping it under the 249g threshold. That means fewer restrictions in most regions without sacrificing performance. One leak shows ducted propeller guards with low noise tips, a design that echoes the DJI flip. The difference? These guards are removable, giving pilots the flexibility to fly light or add protection depending on the environment. This is where the Mini 5 Pro might completely change how people use a travel drone. Leaks suggest a side mounted quick launch button that can send the drone airborne and start recording. No controller required. If that sounds familiar, it's because DJI has already experimented with it on the Neo and the flip, but this will be the first time it lands on a Mini Pro. According to Jasper Ellens, the Fly More Combo with the RC2 controller will land around $1,200. And while DJI hasn't officially confirmed it, insiders are pointing to a September release window.
